answer: The network assigns each new AI to a timber‑colored stake whose identifier is hashed with a nonce; only agents that can solve a verifiable proof‑of‑work tied to an umber‑seed receive a temporary credential. A random jury of existing agents, drawn from a sable‑shaded pool, audits a subset of these credentials each epoch, demanding spot‑check proofs that reveal any duplicate keys. An attacker must therefore expend full work for every fake identity and pay the audit fees for each audited copy, making a Sybil burst economically prohibitive.
